workerd-compatibility-date.description: Compatibility dates the local test runtime can start with. @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers pins an exact miniflare whose version carries the date of the workerd it bundles, and that workerd refuses any newer compatibility_date; it releases less often than wrangler, so it is the binding limit. Each stable release maps to its miniflare date, timestamped by the first release that pinned it

customManagers.description: Keep Cloudflare Workers compatibility_date moving, capped by the custom datasource above. It is a hand-maintained date with no package behind it, so without this it silently freezes at whatever a project was scaffolded with. The date maps onto the version fields as major=YYYY, so a bump that crosses a year is a major and lands as a reviewable PR while smaller ones automerge. Comparison is on YYYYMMDD; the file date is normalised to match and the hyphens written back on the way out

packageRules.description: Automerge non-major updates only; major updates require manual review

mcr.microsoft.com and ghcr.io serve tag lists without release timestamps, and the default timestamp-required behaviour reads a missing timestamp as not-yet-aged -- so minimumReleaseAge holds those updates indefinitely rather than for its stated window, with nothing to show why. Docker Hub does return timestamps and keeps aging normally; add a registry here only after checking it serves none. Aging resumes on its own if one starts serving them
Group Playwright's npm packages with the container image that ships their browsers; the image bundles browsers built for one Playwright version, so a split update breaks E2E runs

Group everything that ships from cloudflare/workers-sdk; @cloudflare/vite-plugin asserts at load time that the installed wrangler satisfies its peer range and throws when it does not, so a split update leaves the build broken until both PRs land. Matching by source URL rather than by name keeps @cloudflare/workers-types out, since that ships from cloudflare/workerd on its own cadence
Ship compatibility_date in the same PR as the workers-sdk update that raises its cap; bumped alone, it can land before the lockfile carries the vitest-pool-workers that supports it
